abstract: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) cardiac MRI enables non-invasive assessment of left atrial (LA) scar, an imaging marker associated with atrial fibrillation ablation outcome. However, automatic scar segmentation is hindered by low contrast, the thin atrial wall, scarce labels, and extreme class imbalance. Conditional diffusion offers iterative mask generation, but its suitability for sparse 3D LA scar segmentation remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose Conditional Mask Diffusion (CMDiff), which predicts clean masks using a dynamic-encoder-conditioned 3D sinusoidal UNet. We compared CMDiff with a deterministic baseline on identical cases in five-fold cross-validation of 60 scar-labelled public LASCARQS subjects, with 48 training and 12 held-out cases per fold. CMDiff achieved a scar DSC of 0.47 $\pm$ 0.08, HD95 of 12.89 $\pm$ 6.39 mm, and ASD of 1.91 $\pm$ 0.96 mm, compared with deterministic baseline values of 0.51 $\pm$ 0.08, 10.86 $\pm$ 5.39 mm, and 1.58 $\pm$ 1.03 mm, respectively. Under the same implementation, clean-mask prediction performed substantially better than the noise-prediction configuration evaluated in this study. Thus, CMDiff was technically feasible but did not improve segmentation performance: DSC was lower, and both HD95 and ASD were higher. Direct mask diffusion therefore provides an analytical alternative, but not a competitive performance advance for this task. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/jizhang02/CMDiff.

sections.body: Left atrial (LA) scar seen on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) MRI is associated with atrial fibrillation ablation outcome. Scar signal sits in the LA wall, roughly 2–4 mm thick, and scar voxels are sparse. The text states that recent anatomy-aware scar segmentation models are deterministic, and that whether a 3D mask-denoising process can recover LA scar directly from LGE-MRI remains unresolved. The authors propose Conditional Mask Diffusion (CMDiff) and compare it with a matched deterministic baseline on identical held-out cases. Contributions are a feasibility and failure-mode study, a clean-mask versus noise-prediction comparison, a Dynamic Conditional Encoder, target, conditioning and sampler ablations, and entropy and variance maps. These metrics are described as repeated-sample variability, not calibrated uncertainty.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Thin, sparse left atrial scar on late gadolinium enhancement MRI makes segmentation hard, so the study tests 3D mask diffusion against a deterministic baseline.

sections.body: CMDiff treats the scar mask as the variable of a conditional diffusion process. Binary masks are mapped to -1 and +1, Gaussian noise is added over T=1000 timesteps with a linear schedule, and a residual 3D UNet with sinusoidal timestep embeddings (SinUNet3D) predicts the clean mask. A Dynamic Conditional Encoder (DCE) adds multi-scale LGE features through FiLM-like modulation, with zero-initialised output layers. Training combines an SNR-weighted MSE diffusion loss with a timestep-weighted soft Dice and weighted binary cross-entropy term, using weights of 0.8 for Dice, 0.2 for BCE and 0.5 for the overall segmentation term. At inference, three soft predictions from random masks are averaged and binarised at zero. Four samplers (DDIM, DPM-Solver++, Euler Discrete, UniPC) are compared across step counts.
sections.heading: Methods
sections.headline: CMDiff denoises a binary scar mask conditioned on the LGE image and predicts the clean mask directly rather than noise.

sections.body: All experiments use the public LASCARQS 2022 dataset. Of 130 subjects with LA anatomy labels, 60 have scar annotations, and separate fixed five-fold partitions are used for each task. Images are resampled to 0.625×0.625×2.5 mm and cropped around the LA, with MONAI augmentations applied. Models train for 3000 epochs on an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU using AdamW, and a 20-step DDIM sampler is used for validation and model selection. Metrics are DSC, HD95 and ASD, with surface distances in millimetres, reported as mean ± standard deviation across held-out subjects. For variability, 20 predictions per held-out case are generated, and entropy and variance are computed inside the foreground. The authors state these are not calibrated error probabilities.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Experiments use five-fold cross-validation on 60 scar-labelled LASCARQS subjects, with 48 training and 12 held-out cases per fold.

sections.body: Table 1 compares prediction targets under matched settings. Noise prediction gives a DSC of 0.0006 and HD95 of 92.6167, while clean-mask prediction gives a DSC of 0.4675 and HD95 of 12.5934. CMDiff has 15.17 million trainable parameters, of which 1.37 M are in the DCE, a 9.0% overhead. The DCE improves DSC in most scheduler settings. For scar, UniPC at 50 steps gives the highest DSC, 0.4687, and 20 steps remains close. Against the deterministic baseline on identical held-out cases, CMDiff has lower scar DSC (0.47 vs. 0.51), higher HD95 (12.89 vs. 10.86 mm) and higher ASD (1.91 vs. 1.58 mm). For LA, CMDiff has lower DSC (0.87 vs. 0.88) and higher ASD (2.07 vs. 1.74 mm), but lower HD95 (7.31 vs. 7.82 mm).
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: Clean-mask prediction gives scar DSC 0.4675 against 0.0006 for noise prediction, but CMDiff trails the deterministic baseline on scar.

sections.body: The clean-mask advantage is reported for the tested loss, timestep weighting, optimisation and scheduler, and the noise-prediction baseline was not independently tuned. Multi-scale conditioning usually improves DSC, while more reverse steps do not consistently improve accuracy. Repeated-sample entropy and variance measure within-model consistency, not segmentation accuracy. The authors argue that explicit anatomy is a more important current lever than stochastic sampling, consistent with the deterministic model's use of LA anatomy as a geometric prior. Three limitations are stated: 60 scar-labelled subjects from one public dataset cannot establish generalisation; iterative inference is substantially slower than a deterministic forward pass; and CMDiff did not use the 70 additional LA-labelled cases or explicitly constrain scar predictions to the LA wall.
sections.heading: Discussion
sections.headline: Conditional diffusion is feasible but not a performance advance here; explicit anatomy is a more important current lever.

sections.body: This feasibility study explored 3D conditional diffusion for left atrial scar segmentation from LGE-MRI. CMDiff learned to generate scar masks with clean-mask prediction, but it did not outperform the matched deterministic baseline in accuracy or efficiency. Both approaches show moderate overlap and remaining surface errors along the thin LA wall. The authors state that the study establishes technical feasibility and identifies failure modes of direct mask diffusion. They motivate future work with larger, high-quality scar-labelled cohorts, and suggest diffusion could refine an initial deterministic segmentation rather than generate the full mask from noise.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The study establishes that direct mask diffusion is technically feasible for LA scar but does not outperform the deterministic baseline.
